cards.hint: identity, origin, what something is

example.es: Soy de México y soy doctora.
example.en: I'm from Mexico and I'm a doctor.

cards.trick: SER sounds like sir: being called sir is part of who you are, your identity.

cards.hint: state, place

example.es: Estoy en casa y muy cansado.
example.en: I'm at home and really tired.

cards.trick: ESTAR sounds like "a star": a star is always somewhere in the sky, shining bright or dim depending on its state.

cards.hint: masculine singular

example.es: El perro está en la cocina.
example.en: The dog is in the kitchen.

cards.trick: EL sounds like the letter L, and L comes before M just like THE comes before a noun.

cards.hint: helper verb, as in I have eaten; not tener

example.en: I've never been to Mexico.

cards.trick: HABER sounds like have-er: it's the helper that turns eaten into have eaten.

cards.hint: as in there is, there are (hay); not estar

example.es: Hay un perro en la casa.
example.en: There is a dog in the house.

cards.trick: HAY sounds like eye: open your eye and see what there is.

example.es: Es la casa de mi mamá.
example.en: It's my mom's house.

cards.trick: DE sounds like day: a cup OF coffee starts the day.

cards.hint: own, possess

example.es: Tengo dos hermanos y un perro.
example.en: I have two brothers and a dog.

cards.trick: TENER sounds like 'tenant': a tenant has a place to live.

cards.hint: used with que before the next verb

example.en: You have to eat something.

cards.trick: TENER QUE sounds like 'ten okay': you have to do ten push-ups before it's okay.

cards.hint: origin

example.en: I'm from Colombia, and you?

cards.trick: DE sounds like day: you came FROM far away, a whole day's trip.

example.es: Mañana voy a la playa con mis amigos.
example.en: Tomorrow I'm going to the beach with my friends.

cards.trick: IR sounds like ear: you go wherever your ear hears music.

example.en: What are you doing tonight?

cards.trick: HACER sounds like 'ah, sir': 'Ah, sir, what should I do?' asks the eager helper.

example.en: I think that she's coming tomorrow.

cards.trick: QUE sounds like "K": that letter K joins two thoughts, just like "that" links them.

example.en: My mom made a cake.

cards.trick: HACER sounds like 'a saucer': you make a saucer out of clay.

cards.hint: can

example.en: Can you help me with this?

cards.trick: PODER sounds like powder: with a little magic powder, you can do anything.

example.es: El hombre que vive aquí es mi tío.
example.en: The man who lives here is my uncle.

cards.trick: QUE sounds like "key": it's the key that points to who or which thing you mean.

example.en: What did you say? I didn't hear you.

cards.trick: DECIR sounds like "the sere": the old seer always has something to say.

cards.hint: facts, information, how to do something

example.es: No sé dónde están mis llaves.
example.en: I don't know where my keys are.

cards.trick: SABER sounds like a wise man's "saber" sword: he cuts through every question because he knows all the answers.

cards.hint: comparing two things

example.es: Mi hermano es más alto que yo.
example.en: My brother is taller than me.

cards.trick: QUE sounds like "K": K comes later in the alphabet than A, so it's "more than" A.

example.en: Do you want a coffee?

cards.trick: QUERER sounds like "carer": a good carer always asks what you want.

cards.hint: family, friends, everyday affection, not amar

example.en: I love you so much, Mom.

cards.trick: QUERER sounds like "care-er": you care about the people you love.

example.en: I'm not hungry.

cards.trick: NO sounds just like English no: put it right before the verb to make anything a no, meaning not.

example.en: Yes, I want to go with you.

cards.trick: SÍ sounds like see: when you see what someone means, you nod and say yes.

cards.hint: in a good way, also fine; not the filler well... (that is bueno)

example.en: You sing really well.

cards.trick: BIEN sounds like "be in": when you're in good shape, you're doing well.

cards.hint: the answer, opposite of yes

example.en: Do you want coffee? No, thanks.

cards.trick: NO is spelled and said like English no, so refusing in Spanish works just like in English.

example.es: No veo nada sin mis lentes.
example.en: I can't see anything without my glasses.

cards.trick: VER sounds like "where": you ask where it is until you finally see it.

cards.hint: a movie, a show (same verb as "to see")

example.en: Should we watch a movie tonight?

cards.trick: VER sounds like "vary": you watch TV and vary the channel all night.

example.es: Tengo un perro y una gata.
example.en: I have a dog and a cat.

cards.trick: UN sounds like oon, a short form of uno (one), so un libro is one book, a book.

example.en: It's a really good movie.

cards.trick: BUENO sounds like "bway-no": no way it's bad, it's good!

cards.hint: filler word to start a reply, not bien

example.en: Well, see you tomorrow.

cards.trick: BUENO starts a reply like "well, now": a quick sound to buy time before you answer.

cards.hint: destination of movement

example.en: Tomorrow I'm going to the beach.

cards.trick: A sounds like 'ah!': you shout 'ah!' as you finally arrive at where you were going.

cards.hint: the standard word, not acá

example.en: Come here, I want to show you something.

cards.trick: AQUÍ sounds like a key: here is a key, right here in my hand.

example.en: I want more coffee, please.

cards.trick: MÁS sounds like "mass": a bigger mass means more.

cards.hint: clock time

example.es: La fiesta empieza a las nueve.
example.en: The party starts at nine.

cards.trick: A sounds like 'ah!': 'Ah, it's eight o'clock!' you gasp, glancing at the clock.

cards.hint: after el or la, as in the most beautiful, not the majority

example.es: Ella es la más inteligente de la clase.
example.en: She is the most intelligent in the class.

cards.trick: MÁS sounds like "mass": whoever has the most mass wins the top spot.

cards.hint: short word, not solamente

example.en: I only want to sleep for a while.

cards.trick: SOLO sounds like a solo song: only one singer, nobody else.

example.es: Tengo un perro y un gato.
example.en: I have a dog and a cat.

cards.trick: Y sounds like "ee": you squeal "eee!" when you get cake and ice cream.

example.en: My grandma lives alone.

cards.trick: SOLO is like Han Solo: a pilot who likes to fly alone.

example.en: I don't believe you at all.

cards.trick: CREER sounds like "career": you need to believe in yourself to build a career.

example.es: Las llaves están en la caja.
example.en: The keys are in the box.

cards.trick: EN sounds like the start of 'inside': whatever is EN something is in it.

cards.hint: believe something is so, as in I think so (not pensar)

example.en: I think it's going to rain.

cards.trick: CREO sounds like "Cray-oh": you draw what you think with a crayon.

cards.hint: must, should; not tener que

example.en: You should call your mom.

cards.trick: DEBER sounds like debate: there is no debate, you simply must do it.

cards.hint: the everyday word, not sobre

example.es: Tu celular está en la mesa.
example.en: Your phone is on the table.

cards.trick: EN is like 'on' with a Spanish accent: the cup sits EN the table.

example.en: I owe you twenty dollars.

cards.trick: DEBER sounds like debt-bear: when you owe money, you bear a debt.

example.en: I already ate, thanks.

cards.trick: YA sounds like a happy "yay": you cheer because it's already done.

cards.hint: location, not direction

example.es: Estoy en el trabajo todo el día.
example.en: I'm at work all day.

cards.trick: EN sounds like the letter N, as in 'Now here': where you are at right now.

cards.hint: two words, before the verb

example.en: I don't live here anymore.

cards.trick: YA NO sounds like "yeah, no": a casual way of saying something doesn't happen anymore.

example.es: Ahora no puedo hablar, estoy ocupado.
example.en: I can't talk now, I'm busy.

cards.trick: AHORA sounds like "a-HOUR-a": the hour that matters is the one happening now (and the Spanish word really does come from hora, hour).

cards.hint: direct object, masculine or it

example.es: Lo vi ayer en la calle.
example.en: I saw him yesterday on the street.

cards.trick: LO sounds like low: you look low and see him lying on the floor.

example.en: The movie is very good.

cards.trick: MUY sounds like a cow's very loud MOO: that cow is very, very noisy.

example.en: Give me the phone, please.

cards.trick: DAR sounds like "dollar": you give someone a dollar.

cards.hint: before an adjective, no noun

example.es: Lo bueno es que llegamos temprano.
example.en: The good thing is that we arrived early.

cards.trick: LO sounds like low: lo bajo is 'the low part', so LO plus an adjective means 'the ... thing' or 'the ... part'.

cards.hint: the everyday word, as in what's happening?

example.en: What happened last night?

cards.trick: PASAR sounds like passer-by: a passer-by always sees what happens on the street.

cards.hint: to go by, go through, or come in

example.es: El autobús pasa por mi casa.
example.en: The bus passes by my house.

cards.trick: PASAR starts like pass: you pass by, pass through, pass the ball.

cards.hint: reason or exchange, not purpose

example.en: Thanks for the help.

cards.trick: POR sounds like pour: you pour out thanks for everything someone did.

cards.hint: time, not money

example.es: Paso los domingos con mi familia.
example.en: I spend Sundays with my family.

cards.trick: PASAR is how you pass the time: you spend the hours letting them pass.

example.en: No, do it like this.

cards.trick: ASÍ sounds like "ah, see?": ah, see? You do it like this.

cards.hint: one short word

example.en: We walk through the park.

cards.trick: POR sounds like pore: sweat goes through your pores.

cards.hint: one word, before an adjective; not medio

example.en: I'm somewhat tired today.

cards.trick: ALGO sounds like 'all go': I'm somewhat tired, but we all go anyway.

cards.hint: leave something or someone behind, not go out

example.es: Dejé las llaves en la mesa.
example.en: I left the keys on the table.

cards.trick: DEJAR sounds like day jar: you leave your coins in the day jar by the door.

example.es: La carta fue escrita por mi papá.
example.en: The letter was written by my dad.

cards.trick: POR sounds like poor: a poem written by a poor poet.

cards.hint: allow, as in let me

example.en: Let me see your phone.

cards.trick: DÉJAME sounds like day, ha, me: let me have the day off, ha!

cards.hint: used with de plus a verb

example.en: My dad quit smoking.

cards.trick: DEJAR DE sounds like day jar day: one day you quit and toss your cigarettes in a jar.

example.en: What are you doing here?

cards.trick: QUÉ sounds like "K?": a puzzled K-shaped question mark asking what.

cards.hint: one occasion, as in one time or many times; not tiempo or hora

example.en: I told you three times.

cards.trick: VEZ sounds like base: every time you touch a base in baseball counts as one more vez.

example.en: Do you speak English?

cards.trick: HABLAR sounds like "blabber": people who blabber talk all day long.

cards.hint: exclamation

example.en: How pretty your house is!

cards.trick: QUÉ sounds like "Kay!": Kay gasps at everything, saying how lovely it all is.

example.en: I feel very tired today.

cards.trick: SENTIR sounds like sent here: every feeling gets sent here, straight to your heart.

cards.hint: the verb in lo siento

example.en: I'm sorry, I can't go.

cards.trick: SIENTO sounds like see an ant, oh: you see the ant you stepped on and say sorry.

cards.hint: object pronoun, attached to or before the verb

example.en: Will you call me tomorrow?

cards.trick: ME is spelled just like English me, so it's an easy one.

example.en: Are you coming to the party tonight?

cards.trick: VENIR sounds like 'when ear': when your ear hears dinner called, you come running.

cards.hint: before a noun: a lot of

example.es: Tengo muchos amigos en la escuela.
example.en: I have a lot of friends at school.

cards.trick: MUCHO sounds like "much-o": it is simply much, with an extra o for more.

cards.hint: reflexive pronoun, goes before the verb

example.es: Me lavo las manos antes de comer.
example.en: I wash my hands before eating.

cards.trick: ME looks like me: when I do something to me, that's myself.

cards.hint: after a verb, as in I eat a lot

example.en: I love you a lot.

cards.trick: MUCHO sounds like "much, oh!": you say it when someone does something a lot.

example.en: Wait for me here, I'll be right back.

cards.trick: ESPERAR sounds like 'is pear ready?': you wait and wait until the pear is ripe.

cards.hint: reflexive pronoun before the verb, also herself, themselves, yourself (usted)

example.es: Mi hermano se levanta muy temprano.
example.en: My brother gets up very early.

cards.trick: SE sounds like 'say': he looks in the mirror and says his name to himself.

example.en: I hope you're well.

cards.trick: ESPERAR sounds like 'aspire': you hope for the things you aspire to.

example.en: I didn't expect to see you here.

cards.trick: ESPERAR sounds like 'prepare': you prepare for whatever you expect to happen.

cards.hint: impersonal: people in general, not a specific you

example.en: How do you say gracias in English?

cards.trick: SE sounds like 'say': how do people say it? ¿Cómo se dice?

example.en: I think about you a lot.

cards.trick: PENSAR sounds like pencil: you chew your pencil while you think hard.

example.en: Thank you very much, you helped me a lot.

cards.trick: GRACIAS sounds like gracious: a gracious person always says thank you.

cards.hint: informal tú, object before the verb

example.en: I'll call you tomorrow.

cards.trick: TE sounds like tea: I'll make you tea because I love you.

cards.hint: polite title or word for a man; feminine señora

example.es: El señor López vive en mi calle.
example.en: Mr. López lives on my street.

cards.trick: SEÑOR sounds like senior: you call an older, respected man sir.

example.es: Tengo muchas cosas que hacer hoy.
example.en: I have a lot of things to do today.

cards.trick: COSA sounds like "cause a": every thing can cause a problem if you leave it lying around.

cards.hint: one short word before the verb

example.en: Did you hurt your hand?

cards.trick: TE sounds like tea: you spilled hot tea on yourself.

example.en: I need your help, please.

cards.trick: NECESITAR sounds like necessity: when something is a necessity, you need it.

example.en: Why are you looking at me like that?

cards.trick: MIRAR sounds like mirror: you look at yourself in the mirror.

example.en: Do you want to come with me or with them?

cards.trick: CON sounds like "cone": ice cream always comes with a cone.

cards.hint: phone, call out

example.es: Te llamo mañana después del trabajo.
example.en: I'll call you tomorrow after work.

cards.trick: LLAMAR starts like llama: picture a llama on the phone, calling you from the Andes.

example.es: Hola, me llamo Ana. ¿Cómo te llamas?
example.en: Hi, my name is Ana. What's your name?

cards.trick: LLAMARSE: a llama introduces itself, saying its name is Larry the Llama.

cards.hint: recipient, purpose or deadline, not por

example.en: This gift is for you.

cards.trick: PARA sounds like a parachute dropping a gift for you, aimed right at its recipient.

example.es: Hoy es un día muy bonito.
example.en: Today is a really nice day.

cards.trick: DÍA sounds like "dear": every new day is dear to me, even though it ends in -a and is still masculine.

example.en: That man is my uncle.

cards.trick: HOMBRE sounds like "OM-bray": picture a man chanting a deep "om" as he walks into the room (the h is silent).

cards.hint: before a verb, showing purpose

example.en: I came to talk to you.

cards.trick: PARA sounds like a paramedic, who rushes in order to save you.

cards.hint: one word, to draw a conclusion or move on, not pues or tan

example.en: So, are you coming or not?

cards.trick: ENTONCES sounds like "in tone, says": in a serious tone, he says, "So, what now?"

cards.hint: at that time, not luego

example.es: Desde entonces, no lo he visto.
example.en: Since then, I haven't seen him.

cards.trick: ENTONCES sounds like "in ton-says": back then, an old clock went ton, ton, and everyone says it.

example.en: My sister lives in Bogotá.

cards.trick: MI sounds like me: anything that belongs to me is my stuff.

example.es: Mi casa tiene un jardín grande.
example.en: My house has a big garden.

cards.trick: CASA sounds like "castle": every house is a little castle to its owner.

cards.hint: as in at home, go home

example.en: I'm going home now.

cards.trick: CASA sounds like "cozy": home is the cozy place you return to.

cards.hint: one word for his, her, their, or formal your

example.en: Her house is very big.

cards.trick: SU sounds like Sue: whose bag is it? It's Sue's, so su means his, her or their.

example.en: Hello! How are you?

cards.trick: HOLA sounds like "hello" with an O and an A: you holler hola to say hello.
